clue.text: Film award winner: The Queen

parts.note: a victor is the one who wins and takes the prize
Victoria was the British queen who reigned 1837-1901

explanation.surface: An announcement that a film's prizewinner is the Queen herself.
explanation.walkthrough: The title is the 1982 Blake Edwards musical comedy starring Julie Andrews.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1982 musical comedy picture with Julie Andrews.

clue.text: Free evenings in, relaxing, finding something for tea

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the order of the three words so their letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spends free evenings at home unwinding with a treat at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxing' rearranges FREE EVENINGS IN. A Viennese finger is a piped butter biscuit, often half-dipped in chocolate, eaten with tea in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Viennese finger is a buttery biscuit commonly served at afternoon teatime.

clue.text: Essential for solver: book rooms

definitions.meaning: a dictionary published by an Edinburgh firm, the crossword solver's standard reference
a set of rooms, especially a barrister's or judge's offices

explanation.definitionFit: The Chambers Dictionary is the crossword setter's and solver's standard reference, and the word also names a suite of private offices.

clue.text: Drink dispenser describes years of Otello?

indicators.note: describes in its geometric sense of drawing round, so the dispenser goes round the years

parts.note: an optic is the measuring device on an upturned spirits bottle in a bar
an era is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A bar's spirit dispenser apparently records the age of an Otello, perhaps a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' means encircles. OPTIC is the British bar device that measures spirits. Otello is Verdi's opera, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Otello is an opera, so anything relating to it belongs to that form of music drama.

clue.text: See 1
Pendant I hook for the sound man

indicators.note: a sound man is a listener here, so the letters are what he hears said

parts.note: I as written, then a sickle, the hook-bladed reaping tool

explanation.surface: An offer of an earring and a hook to a film crew's sound recordist.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'I sickle' becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle hangs down from an edge, and anything hanging that way is pendent, used here as a noun.

clue.text: How brides conventionally marry, without exception

definitions.meaning: traditionally a bride is wed to a husband
an idiom meaning every single one, all together

explanation.definitionFit: A bride traditionally weds a husband, and the same three words form an idiom for everyone, with none excluded.

clue.text: For shapes I book second hour up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Someone making shapes reserves a second hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IBMOHR round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi are the plural of a rhombus, an equal-sided parallelogram, so they are geometric figures.

clue.text: Plate up biscuits for supporting film

indicators.note: in a down entry, the biscuits sit underneath and hold up the first piece
in a down entry, up means the plate's synonym is read from the bottom

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer
crackers are thin crisp savoury biscuits

explanation.surface: Biscuits are plated for a supporting film at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAMINA round. Animal Crackers is a 1930 Marx Brothers comedy; the phrase also names animal-shaped biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1930 Marx Brothers comedy picture.

clue.text: It's in the name: "Laphroaig — the hard stuff"

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A whisky label claims the brand name Laphroaig promises strong spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Laphroaig is an Islay single malt whisky; 'the hard stuff' wants to mean spirits, but it means the hardest substance in the body, on teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooth coating is the hardest substance in the human body.

clue.text: One, not a girl, almost flipping pasta

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole string over so it is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone, not a girl, is nearly losing their temper over pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts GIRL to GIR; 'flipping' turns INOTAGIR round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni are large ridged tubes, a kind of Italian dried noodle.

clue.text: Cut short bigotry in sister from Africa

indicators.note: in places the shortened piece inside the word for the sister

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: cut short removes the last letter of the word for bigotry

parts.note: bias is prejudice, bigotry

explanation.surface: A nun's prejudice is curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia is a historic region of north-east Africa along the Nile, in Sudan and Egypt.

clue.text: Palace supporter seen leaving south London station without top

indicators.note: the supporter is seen going out after, so it comes last
without top means the first letter of the station is dropped

parts.note: Balham is a district in south London with a railway and Tube station
a bra is an undergarment that supports

explanation.surface: A football supporter departs a south London railway station shirtless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without top' drops B from BALHAM. 'Palace' suggests Crystal Palace football club, but it is the Moorish palace in Granada, Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the great Moorish fortress residence at Granada in Spain.

clue.text: Support for log with press

parts.note: and means with, together with
to iron is to press clothes

explanation.surface: A log is held in place by pressing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is a metal firedog that holds burning wood in a hearth.

clue.text: Cannabis-smoker maintaining strength of brew?

definitions.meaning: the extra spoonful of tea leaves added to a teapot to keep the tea strong

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a person keen on marijuana; idiomatically it is the extra spoonful added when brewing tea.

clue.text: One filling pastry dishes in return for passage

indicators.note: filling puts the one inside the turned pastry dishes
in return means the word for the pastry dishes is read backwards

parts.note: tarts are pastry dishes
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A baker fills tarts in exchange for a fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns TARTS into STRAT, and 'filling' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of water between two seas, a sea passage.

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the order follows

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
sixty minutes is an hour, abbreviated hr
taken as written
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A hundred and sixty minutes is the order of the day for a baby's christening.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrisom was the white robe put on a baby at baptism, and by extension the baptized infant itself.

clue.text: Months taken to acquire a woman with a title

indicators.note: the months take on the letter, which joins them at the end

parts.note: Marches is a plural of March, a month

explanation.surface: It takes months for someone to gain a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchesa is an Italian noblewoman, wife of a marquis.

clue.text: Where Spooner makes tired house visit

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: worn means tired, worn out
a call is a visit to someone's house

explanation.surface: A Spooner-style mangling of a weary doctor's home visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's far south-west tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall is a county in south-west England, so it answers a question about place.

clue.text: See 8
Drum leader of party out — after time

indicators.note: after means the trimmed party follows the letter for time
the leader of the party's name is its first letter, which goes out

parts.note: Labour is a major British political party

explanation.surface: A drummer leads a party out on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' completes 'leader of ... out', removing L from LABOUR. Labour is a major British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabour is a small drum played with one hand while piping with the other.

clue.text: See 1
The first person strangely isn't you, in the end located as intended

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the word before it are rearranged
in the end picks only the final letter of the word you

explanation.surface: Someone insists that the first person is not you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges ISNT to NSIT; 'in the end' takes the last letter of YOU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its original or proper place.

clue.text: It's easy to sound out French cheeses

indicators.note: sounding out a word is saying it aloud

parts.note: Bries are soft cheeses from France

explanation.surface: Pronouncing French cheese names is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is something done with no trouble at all.

clue.text: See 13
Enthusiast dismissed spread

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
out means dismissed, as a batter is in cricket

explanation.surface: A supporter is sent packing and spread out.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan out is to spread across a wider area, like opening a hand of cards.

clue.text: Inside article about male soul

parts.note: inner means inside
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article on the inner life of men.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's inner self, the spiritual side, is their soul.

clue.text: One geometrical curve representing a figure

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a conic is a curve from slicing a cone, such as an ellipse

explanation.surface: A geometry student draws a single curve to depict a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is an image or emblem, standing for a person or symbol.

clue.text: I've lead in lead

parts.note: the speaker takes the lead, while being held on a leash; lead is sounded differently twice

explanation.definitionFit: A dog trained to steer a blind owner walks in front and is held on a harness.

clue.text: Fighting in insect cave

indicators.note: in places the fighting inside the insect

parts.note: a bee is an insect
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Fighting inside an insect's cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' is the Latin warning 'look out', used in English schoolboy slang, not a hollow in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin 'cave' is a warning to look out, so it equals a caution to take care.

clue.text: Better to use all, in rotation?

definitions.text: Better to use all, in rotation?

parts.words: Better to use all, in rotation?
parts.note: a better is a gambler; the place where all bets are laid while a wheel spins

explanation.definitionFit: Gamblers place their stakes on these casino tables while the wheel revolves.
